title: How to (Accidentally) Spot an Islamabad IT Guy. Tip #1
body: He works in I-9 or I-10 in a building that looks like a plaza because it is a plaza. Ask the company. Systems, Contour, S&P, Motive, Xgrid, or a software house nobody outside the sector has heard of, and he will describe all of them as "a product company." Ask what he does. If the answer is "backend" and nothing else, correct. If he tells you the salary out loud, he's junior or lying. It's a sealed deal if the office has a foosball table nobody has touched since orientation.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot an Islamabad IT Guy. Tip #2
body: Ask what currency he's paid in and watch the whole personality arrive. Rupees is a job. Dollars is a career. If he starts explaining the dollar rate unprompted, he's paid in dollars and needs you to know. Every Islamabad developer tracks the interbank rate like a sports score. It's a sealed deal if he has ever timed a withdrawal to the rate and told the story more than once.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot an Islamabad IT Guy. Tip #3
body: Ask about the exit plan, because there is always an exit plan with a country attached. Dubai, Germany, Canada, Australia, and each one has a batchmate who already went and posts about the weather. He has a spreadsheet. He has looked at the points calculator at 2am more than once. It's a sealed deal if he knows the IELTS band he needs and the one he actually got.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot an Islamabad IT Guy. Tip #4
body: Listen to the language. Urdu with the guard, Urdu-English in standup, and every technical noun in English with no exceptions. "Deploy kar diya," "merge ho gaya," "bug hai." Nobody has said these in Urdu and nobody will. If his mother describes his job to relatives as "computer pe kaam karta hai," that's the standard, nobody has improved on it. It's a sealed deal if a khala has asked him to fix her phone at a wedding.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot an Islamabad IT Guy. Tip #5
body: Watch what happens after work. Gym at 9, chai at Rana Market at 11, and a drive down Margalla Road with the windows down because there is nowhere to go and everyone knows it. Islamabad has no nightlife so the drive is the nightlife. It's a sealed deal if he has a specific loop through the city he drives when he's thinking and it takes forty minutes.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot an Islamabad IT Guy. Tip #6
body: Ask about the side project. There is one. It has been in progress for two years, it has a domain he renews faithfully, and he has never shown it to anyone. Ask to see it and watch him refuse with real feeling. It's a sealed deal if he has bought a domain for a company that does not exist and still pays for it every year.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot an Islamabad IT Guy. Tip #7
body: Look at the commute. He lives in G-11 or I-8 and works in I-9, which is eleven minutes, and he will still complain about traffic. If he lives in Bahria and works in Blue Area, he has accepted a ninety-minute life and reorganised his entire day around it. It's a sealed deal if he knows exactly which minute to leave the house and treats it as non-negotiable.
